Generalized synthetic control with interactive fixed effects

Source: R/ifx.R
ifesc.Rd

The effect of a treatment adopted by some units of a balanced panel at possibly different times, estimated as the generalized synthetic control of Xu (2017): a model of the untreated outcome fitted to the units never treated, then carried to each treated unit through its periods before adoption.

Usage

ifesc(
  data,
  y,
  d,
  unit,
  time,
  x = NULL,
  r = NULL,
  rmax = 5,
  se = c("boot", "none"),
  nboot = 200,
  seed = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  tol = 1e-08,
  maxit = 1000
)

# S3 method for class 'ifesc'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ifesc'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit and time (balanced: every unit at every time once).

y

The name of the outcome column (numbers).

d

The name of the treatment column: 0 or 1 (or FALSE, TRUE), staying 1 once it turns 1; never-treated units are the controls.

unit, time

The names of the unit column (labels) and the time column (numbers or dates; ordered by value).

x

NULL or the names of covariate columns (numbers).

r

NULL (cross-validation) or the number of factors, a whole number from 0.

rmax

The largest number of factors cross-validation tries.

se

"boot" (the bootstrap of units) or "none".

nboot

The number of bootstrap draws, at least 2.

seed

NULL (the generator's current state) or one whole number.

level

The confidence level of the intervals.

tol

The convergence tolerance of b.

maxit

The most alternations of Bai's estimator.

...

Not used by print() and summary(); for plot(), passed to the base-graphics call.

object

An object of class ifesc.

Value

An object of class ifesc, a list: att, a one-row data frame (est, se, stat, p, lo, hi); eff, one row per event time e (n treated units observed then, and the same columns); r; cv, a data frame of r and mspe (NULL when r was given); beta, the covariates' coefficients; cf, one row per treated unit and time (unit, time, e, y, y0, eff); factors, T x r; draws, the bootstrap's att then eff per draw, a row each (NULL for se = "none"); ntr, nco, nt; iter, conv; nboot, nfail, level. summary() returns eff.

Details

The untreated outcome of unit i at time t is y_it = x_it'b + mu + alpha_i + xi_t + lambda_i'f_t + e_it, the interactive fixed effects model of Bai (2009): unit and time effects plus r common factors f_t with unit loadings lambda_i, which let units follow different trends (a difference in differences assumes r = 0). On the never-treated units the estimator of Bai (2009) alternates the factors, sqrt(T) times the first r eigenvectors of W W' for the doubly demeaned residuals W net of covariates (normalised F'F / T = I), and b, by least squares of the doubly demeaned outcome less the common component on the doubly demeaned covariates, until b changes by less than tol. Each treated unit's alpha_i and lambda_i come from least squares of its residuals on (1, f_t) over its periods before adoption, which must number more than r + 1; its counterfactual y0 is the model's value at every period, and its effect at a period is y - y0. att averages the effects of the treated periods; eff averages them by periods since adoption (event time e, 0 the first treated period; the effects before adoption are the fit's in-sample gaps).

r = NULL chooses the number of factors from 0 to rmax by the cross-validation of Xu (2017, sec. 3.1, algorithm 1): each treated unit's pre-adoption periods are left out one at a time, the loadings fitted on the rest and the left-out outcome predicted; the r with the smallest mean squared prediction error is kept (cv). The search stops at the first r some treated unit has too few periods for.

The standard errors are those of a bootstrap of units, the "simple nonparametric bootstrap" Xu (2017, sec. 3.2, p. 63) finds valid when the treated units are many: each draw takes as many units as the panel has, with replacement, and refits with the chosen r; draws with no treated unit or with no more control units than r fail and are left out. With few treated units Xu (2017) prefers a parametric bootstrap that resamples residuals, which is not built here. Rows of a unit drawn twice enter twice.

Barber (2026) estimates the effect of the New York City congestion charge on fine particles, traffic speeds and arrests with the generalized synthetic control, and the spatial shift of arrests with a difference in differences (see didfe()).

References

Bai, J. (2009). Panel data models with interactive fixed effects. Econometrica, 77(4), 1229-1279. doi:10.3982/ECTA6135

Xu, Y. (2017). Generalized synthetic control method: causal inference with interactive fixed effects models. Political Analysis, 25(1), 57-76. doi:10.1017/pan.2016.2

Barber, T. J. (2026). The New York City congestion charge: air quality, traffic, and crime. MS thesis, Cornell University.

Examples

set.seed(1)
p <- expand.grid(id = 1:30, yr = 1:12)
f <- cumsum(rnorm(12))
l <- rnorm(30)
p$tr <- as.integer(p$id <= 6 & p$yr >= 9)
p$y <- l[p$id] * f[p$yr] + 2 * p$tr + rnorm(nrow(p), 0, 0.3)
r <- ifesc(p, "y", "tr", "id", "yr", r = 1, nboot = 50, seed = 1)
r
#> ifesc: generalized synthetic control, 6 treated and 24 control units, 12 times, 1 factor(s)
#>    est     se  stat         p    lo    hi
#>  1.994 0.2222 8.974 2.851e-19 1.558 2.429
